item.title: UAE accuses Iran of Hormuz attacks as Vance says cheap gas is "goal number one"
item.description: The United Arab Emirates blamed Iran for attacks on two vessels linked to its state-owned oil company as they passed through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Warship that sank in 1908 found off U.K.: "Undisturbed for 118 years"
item.description: The Royal Navy and shipwreck hunters have been searching in vain for the remains of HMS Tiger for over a century.

item.title: Does Mangione's guilty plea in federal case jeopardize state murder trial?
item.description: Luigi Mangione pleaded guilty to two federal counts on Friday. His state trial is currently scheduled to begin on Sept. 8.

item.title: Luigi Mangione pleads guilty in federal case, admits shooting Brian Thompson
item.description: Luigi Mangione entered a guilty plea in his federal case at a court appearance in Manhattan Friday morning.

item.title: United Kingdom's Nigel Farage wins special election against trash can-themed opponent, Count Binface
item.description: Nigel Farage regained his U.K. Parliament seat, beating comedian candidate Count Binface in a farcical special election. BBC News' Joe Pike reports.

item.title: Brian Thompson's family reacts after Luigi Mangione says he will plead guilty in federal case
item.description: The family of slain UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson is reacting to news that his alleged killer, Luigi Mangione, plans to plead guilty in the federal case against him. CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson has more.

item.title: Hawaii under a hurricane warning as Tropical Storm Lala takes aim
item.description: Tropical Storm Lala could bring heavy rain, high winds and dangerous surf and rip currents to the Hawaiian Islands as a hurricane this weekend, forecasters say.

item.title: Violent crime plummeted in U.S. last year, White House official says
item.description: The White House is touting a historic drop in violent crime as the FBI prepares to release the latest data from its annual Uniform Crime Reporting Program.

item.title: Inside "the Pool": Fugitive arrested in alleged cross-border car trade scheme
item.description: Along the Texas-Mexico border, prosecutors say a group of businessmen found a way to monopolize the trade of used cars — a scheme called "the Pool." This week, authorities say they caught one alleged member.

item.title: Thinking about a gold IRA? Here's what you need to know first.
item.description: A gold IRA can add precious metals to your retirement plan, but there's a lot to consider before opening one.

item.title: What to expect as Tropical Storm Lala nears Hawaii's Big Island
item.description: Tropical Storm Lala could bring strong winds and heavy rain to Hawaii over the next few days. Michael Brennan, a NOAA Hurricane Center director, has more on what to expect.

item.title: Officials react to Luigi Mangione's plan to plead guilty in federal case
item.description: United States Attorney Jamie McDonald and New York City Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch spoke to reporters after a court hearing where Luigi Mangione revealed he plans to plead guilty in the federal case against him for the death of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson. Katrina Kaufman and Tom Hanson have more.

item.title: Lacrosse power couple Taylor Moreno and Ally Kennedy enjoy their own "Heated Rivalry"
item.description: California Palms goalkeeper Taylor Moreno and Maryland Charm midfielder Ally Kennedy are rivals on the lacrosse field and partners off of it. This athletic power couple shares their thoughts on the inaugural Women's Lacrosse League championship.

item.title: Justice Department expands military's power to detain migrants near border
item.description: The Justice Department issued a legal opinion giving the U.S. military broader powers to detain migrants near certain areas along the southern border.

item.title: Luigi Mangione's lawyer speaks out after he announced plans to plead guilty in federal case
item.description: Karen Friedman Agnifilo, Luigi Mangione's attorney, spoke to reporters outside a New York City federal court, where he told a judge that he plans to plead guilty in his federal case. CBS News' Tom Hanson and Katrina Kaufman report.

item.title: French teen social media ban struck down by top constitutional authority
item.description: France's social media ban, which was due to take effect on Sept. 1, would have barred younger users from networks such as TikTok, Snapchat and Instagram.

item.title: U.S. and Iran in "deadlock" as both claim control of Stait of Hormuz, expert says
item.description: Iran and the U.S. are sending out contrasting messages about the future of the Strait of Hormuz. Mona Yacoubian of the Middle East Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies weighs in.

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Aug. 16)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Book excerpt: Modesty on the line in "The Summer of Death"
item.description: Geoff Williams' account of the deadly heat wave of 1936 includes one Kentucky city's efforts to arrest young women whose warm-weather attire was considered too revealing.

item.title: Pearl Jam frontman Eddie Vedder looks to help kids with rare "butterfly" skin disease
item.description: Pearl Jam's Eddie Vedder is pushing to help kids with Epidermolysis Bullosa, a condition where children suffer from fragile, painful "butterfly" skin. Dr. Céline Gounder shares more about rare childhood diseases and research efforts.

item.title: Lottery frenzy hits Illinois town where winning billion-dollar Powerball ticket was sold
item.description: Excitement has reached a fever pitch in Quincy, the Illinois town where the winning billion-dollar Powerball jackpot ticket was sold. CBS News' Lana Zak checked out the convenience store that sold the lucky ticket.

item.title: American missionary kidnapped in Niger in October is freed
item.description: An American missionary who was kidnapped in Niger in October has been released, his organization says, adding that Kevin Rideout "is in good health in the care of U.S. officials."

item.title: Inside Russia's alleged plot to murder a dual U.S.-Ukrainian citizen in Poland
item.description: Prime Minister Donald Tusk says Polish authorities foiled Russia's attempt to assassinate a Ukrainian-American dual citizen. CBS News' Ramy Inocencio explains what we know.

item.title: Reports of dire conditions, mental health crises on USS Abraham Lincoln
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth rejected reports of poor conditions on the Navy's USS Abraham Lincoln, saying that conditions have been "completely misrepresented." CBS News' Zak Hudak reports.

item.title: USS Washington aircraft carrier heads to Middle East to replace USS Lincoln
item.description: The USS George Washington aircraft carrier departed Vietnam last week and is headed to the Middle East to replace the USS Abraham Lincoln, according to a U.S. official.

item.title: Indiana river breaks 1913 flooding record as governor declares state of emergency
item.description: The White River in Indiana rose to record-breaking levels as more than 11 inches of rain has fallen east of Indianapolis since Tuesday.

item.title: See how much renters pay for a 2-bedroom home in 50 U.S. cities
item.description: Nearly half of renters spend more than 30% of their income on housing. Here's what it costs to rent a two-bedroom home in 50 U.S. cities.

item.title: 2 killed as Apache helicopter from Fort Hood crashes in Salado, Texas
item.description: Two soldiers aboard an AH-64 Apache attack helicopter based out of Fort Hood were killed in a crash on Wednesday, according to local authorities and the Army.

item.title: Treating Lindsay Clancy | Case by Case | "48 Hours" Podcast
item.description: The focus in the Lindsay Clancy trial shifts to her mental health treatment as jurors hear testimony from her psychiatric providers, friends, and family. "48 Hours" correspondent Erin Moriarty and CBS News correspondent Shanelle Kaul break down the emotional moments in court, the competing narratives emerging at the center of the case, and the lasting questions surrounding maternal mental health.

item.title: My husband was kicked out of hospice. Here's what I learned.
item.description: Some seriously ill patients improve on hospice. About 1 in 16 patients enrolled in hospice care lose eligibility as a result. Here's how to get appropriate care.
